metadata.title: Tajemnica Starego Zamku
metadata.author: AI Composer
metadata.description: Title theme in the classic Polish 1980s 8-bit adventure game style (evoking LK Avalon and Mirage Software). Combines a proud, rustic medieval motif with mischievous fantasy swagger.

form_plan.primary_theme_description: Theme A: Stately yet slightly rustic D minor march with a bouncy heroic motif, driving chiptune bass, and playful counter-arpeggios.
form_plan.contrast_theme_description: Theme B: Mischievous F major/G dorian divertimento, characterized by syncopated call-and-response and humorous staccato ornamentations.

sections.description: Rustic fanfaric call in D minor with rising staccato bass pulses.
Full heroic main melody on Channel 0, walking bass on Channel 1, arpeggiated support on Channel 2, and rhythmic noise percussion on Channel 3.
Theme A continuing with more adventurous melodic leaps and octave embellishments.
Humorous, mischievous B theme in relative major/dorian with bouncy rhythms and sudden dynamic drops.
Theme B escalation with rapid lead ornaments and driving percussion leading back to D minor.
Triumphant return of the main heroic adventure theme.
Climactic restatement with full energy and resolved cadence.
Humorous concluding flourish with a definitive Picardy third cadence.

patterns.texture_notes: Sparse opening call building into full ensemble rhythm.
Main adventurous theme with full 4-voice Polish 8-bit orchestration.
Second phrase of Theme A with complete tonic resolution in D minor.
Playful, light-footed B section with oom-pah style chiptune accompaniment.
Dramatic escalation and harmonic turnaround preparing the heroic Theme A restatement.
Triumphant final cadential flourish resolving with a warm Picardy D major third.

intent.composition_notes: Crafted with authentic POKEY polyphonic voice leading. Features a gallant Slavic minor theme on Channel 0, punchy monophonic basslines on Channel 1, airy counterpoint on Channel 2, and energetic noise percussion accents on Channel 3. The 8 patterns of 64 steps at 125 BPM produce an exact runtime of 61.44 seconds.
